Subject: Upgrade gating matrix & rollback ownership — MeridianCloud private deployment

Team / Meridian Ops,

We need to lock in the upgrade plan for MeridianCloud's private deployment next month. Goal: perform the 2.4.1 -> 2.5.0 minor upgrade with minimal disruption and a clear, testable rollback path.

Proposed immediate asks:
- Review the attached gating matrix (upgrade-gating-matrix-v1.xlsx) and confirm any missing technical gates.
- Confirm a maintenance window (target 2028-06-15 02:00-06:00 UTC or an equivalent that fits Meridian's low-traffic period).
- Identify who owns each rollback action (pin/unpin, DB migratory steps, KV cache invalidation, network route revert).

High-level constraints:
- We must be able to pin to 2.4.1 in < 30 minutes from decision.
- KV cache should be drain-only during upgrade (no writes).
- Any schema migration must be entirely backward-compatible or feature-flagged.

Attaching the gating matrix draft. Monica — can you run the compliance checklist (audit logs, KMS access) and note any gaps? Dev / Karthik — please add any executable gating steps and estimated times. Meridian — can you confirm the feasibility of the window above and whether an SLA exception is needed?

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: upgrade-gating-matrix-v1.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upgrade gating matrix & rollback ownership — MeridianCloud private deployment

Kimberly,

Thanks — skimmed the matrix and made inline notes. Key technical gates I'd add (high level):

1) Preflight smoke on staging with identical KV warm cache (30m): verify prefix-eviction, cold-start latency.
2) KV drain procedure (10m): set writes to backend-only, wait for inflight tokens to finish, snapshot keys.
3) Binary pin/unpin checklist (15m):
   - Disable autoscaler triggers to avoid new nodes joining mid-upgrade.
   - Signal runtime to stop accepting new inference sessions.
   - Confirm model weights checksum and deploy artifact id.
4) Kernel compatibility check (5m): ensure quantization kernel set loaded for 2.5.0 or fallback branch exists.
5) Telemetry gating (continuous): token latency P50/P95 within 25% of baseline for first 15m of traffic.

Rollback notes:
- The fastest rollback is to pin the fleet to the prior artifact (2.4.1) and drain new nodes. That requires network-level routing rollback and a small DNS TTL change (we should avoid DNS where possible; prefer internal L3 route flip).
- We'll need a db read-only switch if we detect schema drift.

I've pushed comments to the Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/meridian-upgrades (see folder /tech-preflight).

Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Sara / Team,

Adding the roll-forward and rollback play definitions I mentioned in the last eng sync. Please find the short runbook summary below — I'll drop a full draft to the Drive as rollback-runbook-draft.md.

Rollback decision tree (condensed):
- If P50 latency > 2x baseline OR error-rate spike > 5% for 5min -> trigger rollback.
  Action: pin fleet to 2.4.1 artifact id -> initiate route flip back to pre-upgrade subnet -> scale down 2.5.0 nodes. Expected time: 20–30m.
- If progressive degradations only on a subset of racks -> isolate racks via BGP community tag, failover traffic to warm spares. Expected time: 15–40m depending on BGP convergence.

Ownership: (proposed)
- Pin/unpin artifact: Dev Patel (runtime)
- Network route flip: Meridian Ops (Sara / Rafael)
- DB read-only toggle & migration rollback: Monica Patel
- Observability/alert clear: Karthik Iyer

I also recommend a 30-minute post-rollback observation before re-trying the upgrade.

Karthik
Principal, Inference Reliability
